name: og-vent-interface
title: The Evolving Mineral Interface: A Bounded DIC Window
concept: The evolving mineral-water interface: whether a coupled geochemical interface sustains its H2 / inorganic-carbon flux and a maintained pH/redox gradient as the minerals evolve — and where it throttles. Builds on the calibrated vent states of og-vent-environment (1A).
gate_reason: Evolving-interface half of the former og-vent-environment (split from the calibrated-states half). Canonical arm og-27. HONEST STATUS: qualified on the one REALIZED result, the bounded two-regime DIC window (og27-dic-crossover-bounded-window; the dic-crossover-sweep primary passes, window_exists=False). Its other five og-27 findings (sustained reactive flux, mineral-evolution supply decay, electrochemical driving force, coupled conservation ledger, handoff-to-29) remain status:planned — not yet realized. Carries plan_id 27 and the numeric refs to study 27.
claim: The evolving mineral interface delivers reduced-carbon chemistry only within a bounded two-regime DIC window — under full redox equilibrium, DIC is drawn down before free H2 appears, so the usable window is narrow (og27-dic-crossover-bounded-window; dic-crossover-sweep passes). Qualified: this DIC-cliff is the realized result; sustained-flux, mineral-evolution supply decay and the coupled ledger over timescales are scaffolded (planned), not yet run.
question: Does the evolving mineral-water interface sustain its H2 / inorganic-carbon flux and pH/redox gradient as minerals evolve, and where does the DIC window bound it?
hypothesis: The coupled interface maintains a usable reduced-carbon feed only inside a bounded DIC window, with a sharp two-regime crossover where free H2 and dissolved inorganic carbon trade off.
experiment: Sweep the coupled geochemical reaction interface (og-27) across the DIC crossover to bound the window (realized); the sustained-flux / mineral-evolution / coupled-ledger tests over timescales are specified but PLANNED, not yet run.
result: A bounded two-regime DIC window: under full redox equilibrium DIC is reduced before free H2 appears, so the usable reduced-carbon window is narrow (dic-crossover-sweep passes, window_exists=False). Qualified on this realized DIC-cliff; the remaining og-27 flux / mineral-evolution / ledger findings are planned.

arms.concept_role: Canonical (sharpened coupled interface): the evolving mineral-water interface delivers H2 / inorganic-carbon flux + a maintained pH/redox gradient at or above required levels and a CO2-reducing electrochemical driving force, with mass/charge/energy closing across PHREEQC+FiPy+Reaktoro — BUT precipitation + surface passivation throttle catalytic supply on the mineral-evolution timescale and the supply<->throttle is a sharp two-regime DIC cliff, so delivery is bounded/conditional (QUALIFIED).

behavior_tests.name: dic-crossover-sweep
behavior_tests.description: A dense fluid_dic sweep across the PHREEQC SI=0 crossover characterizes the supply-vs-throttle two-regime behavior and whether any operating point sustains flux AND exercises throttling with the pore open (the calibration that resolves needs_calibration).

measure.detail: H2 flux / precipitation / accessibility / porosity vs fluid_dic across SI=0

pass_if.detail: the crossover is characterized with the ledger closing at every point (window_exists resolved either way)

findings.evidence_basis_note: The sharp two-regime DIC cliff is a real-PHREEQC model finding.
findings.statement: The interface's supply↔throttle behavior is a sharp two-regime cliff, not a gradual depletion: across a dense fluid_dic sweep (2–20 mM) real PHREEQC carbonate saturation crosses SI=0 at ~3.2 mM, and the interface either SUPPLIES (undersaturated, SI<0: H2 flux 2.75e-4 → 3.55e-5 from 2.0 → 3.0 mM, no precipitation, pore open at porosity 0.96–0.97) OR THROTTLES-AND-CHOKES (supersaturated, SI≥+0.7: precipitation 0.23–0.29 and catalytic-accessibility drop ~0.12, but H2 flux crashes four orders to ~1e-8 and porosity collapses to 0) — never both. No fluid_dic sustains flux AND exercises throttling with the pore open (window_exists=False), so the self-limiting carbonate chemistry forces the vent operating point into the undersaturated regime. The free-energy/mass/charge ledger closes at every sweep point.

Over transport timescales the interface delivers H2 and inorganic-carbon fluxes and a maintained pH/redox gradient at or above the levels used by published vent-reactor and H2-dependent-metabolism work; the study reports the full time series and the onset of decay, not a single terminal value.

Precipitation and surface passivation reduce reactive surface and throttle catalytic supply on the mineral-evolution timescale — the interface is depleting, and the study quantifies the crossover time at which delivery drops below the downstream-required threshold.

The cross-interface electrical driving force is non-trivial and of the sign/scale needed to drive CO2 reduction, verified independently by a FEniCSx Nernst–Planck solve against the FiPy transport result.
Mass, charge and energy close across the coupled PHREEQC+FiPy+Reaktoro solve to tolerance with no untracked feeds.

The study emits the full 27→29 transfer bundle — H2 + inorganic-carbon flux, pH, T, ionic activities, catalyst (mineral-surface) state and time-dependent feeds — as the typed boundary condition study 29 consumes.

sustained-reactive-flux-over-timescales.detail: H2 source flux sustained (0 -> 2.74e-4 mol/s) over the transport timescale; conservation holds.

mineral-evolution-supply-decay.detail: Undersaturated dissolution regime (saturation_index -15..-17); porosity opens 0.35->0.98, mineral_precipitation=0, catalytic_accessibility stays 1 - throttling criterion unexercised at this operating point.

dic-crossover-sweep.detail: Characterized the real PHREEQC SI=0 cliff at ~3.2 mM fluid_dic; window_exists=False (no fluid_dic sustains flux AND throttles with the pore open); ledger closes at every swept point - the calibration that resolves needs_calibration.

mineral-evolution-supply-decay.detail: Throttling now EXERCISED across the supersaturated band (precipitation 0.23-0.29, catalytic-accessibility drop ~0.12, porosity -> 0) - the criterion the undersaturated default point could not exercise.

coupled-conservation.detail: Mass/charge/energy ledger closes at every swept fluid_dic (ledger_ok_all=True).

config.title: The interface evolves — supply vs self-throttling
config.caption: Top row — outlet temperature, pH and H2 flux: the conditions and reducing power the vent wall delivers. Bottom row — porosity closing, catalytic accessibility passivating, and carbonate saturation index driving precipitation. Plainly: the wall delivers chemistry at first, but as minerals grow and clog it that delivery declines — the interface depletes rather than lasting forever.
